findings.title: A killed source generation can let an in-flight reader store a wrong out-degree
findings.intended: ADJ-I5.9 / ADJ-I5.9.1; HD-0401 (assumption): invalidation never makes an old degree-cache value valid again.
findings.remedy: Per HD-0401: step the generation (or a graph epoch) and never kill it; the model also needs the step before the write (see F-C0401).
findings.notes: adj_degree-as-built-F0401-erase gives the finding's trace; the refinement audit against L1 'degree = committed out count' fails as built and passes for the reviewed design. Live provocation is unrepresentable with the public surface: the window lies between the probe and the count inside one Adj.Degree call. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-model to intent-undecided. The intended behaviour rests only on HD-0401, an Assumption (decisions.md: 'invalidation can never make an old degree-cache value valid again' is the working choice; a per-source generation is named as an alternative) and on ADJ-I5.9, which restates it; no authoritative source settles it. The observed behaviour is unchanged and kept: as-built model breadth-a-mc-adj_degree-as-built and the located control proofs-breadth-hd0401-erase-kills-gen reproduce the trace (model-level; not provoked live). Conditional on HD-0401: a defect if the maintainer adopts it.
findings.observed: Adj.Degree's four steps (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adj.cls:51-90) against RemoveSource/RemoveGraph/RemoveAll killing ^KG('gen') (Adjacency.cls:376-377, 437-438, 461-462) and a rolled-back erase.

findings.title: A rebuilt store or cached answer can stay current after the write it read is rolled back
findings.intended: AlgoCache.cls:5-7 ('never wrongly fresh'); ADR-0012:23-26 names the case unsafe; ADJ-I7.3 / ADJ-I11.2.
findings.remedy: Probe the writer lock exclusively before computing and store only if the probe held and the token did not move, AND step the token before the adjacency write: the model shows the probe alone leaves a writer-stopped-mid-write window (adj_token-probe-writer-window).
findings.notes: Live: token 114 -> 115 by the open write, WCC computed and cached under 115, writer rolled back (row and out entry gone), token stays 115, a fresh engine's kg_WCC was a cache hit joining the rolled-back edge's endpoints.

observed.verdict: cache entry stamped with the rolled-back write's token served the rolled-back edge
observed.oracle: after W's rollback no current cached answer includes W's edge

findings.title: A failed adjacency rebuild inside a caller's transaction rolls back the caller's work
findings.intended: CHANGELOG 4.6.4 (CHANGELOG.md:410-424): an IVG write never commits or rolls back a transaction its caller opened.
findings.remedy: Roll back to the level found, or refuse sync() inside a caller transaction.
findings.notes: Precondition: the engine's Native API handle shares the caller's process (an engine built on the caller's DB-API connection, as here); on a from_connect engine BuildKG runs in another process.

observed.verdict: failed sync ended the caller's transaction and discarded its node
observed.oracle: the caller's transaction and its writes survive a failed IVG call made inside it

findings.title: A writer stopped between its adjacency write and its generation step lets a reader cache a count that includes the undone edge
findings.intended: ADJ-I5.9 / ADR-0012: a cached degree carrying the current generation equals the committed count.
findings.remedy: Step the generation before the out write (the reviewed adj_degree design), as well as never killing it (HD-0401).
findings.notes: New, from the model sub-lane. The same window exists as built (Put's order is unchanged in HD-0401's fix). Not provoked live: needs a process stopped between two statements of one class method.
findings.observed: Adjacency.Put writes ^KG('out')/('in') and only then $Increments ^KG('gen') (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls:87-89); Adj.Degree's probe can precede the writer's lock and its count can follow the out write (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adj.cls:68-80). A writer process stopped between the two (rolled back by IRIS, P-0001) leaves the generation unchanged, so the reader's store of the dirty count stays current.

findings.title: Two adjacency rebuilds can run at once
findings.intended: HD-0402 (assumption): at most one publishing rebuild per adjacency structure; the ADMIN_GUIDE names a single rebuild.
findings.remedy: Take the rebuild lock exclusively (or a separate exclusive rebuild lock) and return busy to a second caller.
findings.notes: New. Check adj_rebuild_txn-concurrent-as-built-HD0402 violates ADJ-Q8.10; the reviewed exclusive design passes; control early-release is caught. Intent rests on HD-0402, an assumption. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-model to intent-undecided. The record's own intent rests on HD-0402, an Assumption ('a proven concurrent generation swap would also satisfy the objective', decisions.md); the ADMIN_GUIDE naming a single rebuild does not forbid two. Observed behaviour kept: adj_rebuild_txn-concurrent-as-built-HD0402 violates ADJ-Q8.10 in the model. Conditional on HD-0402. The overlap itself stays recorded as the violated breadth-proof premise P-A4.
findings.observed: Adjacency.BeginRebuild takes ^IVG.AdjW in shared mode (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls:814-822), which a second rebuild's shared request does not conflict with (P-0403).

findings.title: Candidate: with the adjacency index declared, a failed rebuild could leave part of the adjacency missing
findings.intended: TraversalBuild.BuildKG's comment (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/TraversalBuild.cls:46-55): the kill sits inside the transaction so a row the rebuild cannot process leaves the adjacency as it was, never destroyed.
findings.remedy: Build the new adjacency beside the old one and publish it atomically, or keep the indexed path's purge inside a transaction it can roll back (no parallel jobs), or validate every row's graph key before purging.
findings.notes: Candidate from the journal (J12: ^KG out/in refilled outside any transaction by the caller's and two worker processes) against the method's comment: the indexed path purges and refills after TCommit with %BuildIndices in parallel jobs. Not reproduced: a sync() failed on a row with graph_id '0' left all 400 sources of a 400-edge graph in ^KG out and verify_graph ok. Readers during the refill can still see a partial adjacency (the method's own catch comment says so); that window was not measured. Not counted as a defect.

observed.verdict: adjacency intact after the failed rebuild
observed.oracle: TraversalBuild.cls:46-55: a row the rebuild cannot process leaves the adjacency as it was
